titre: Studying the Effluent Quality of Enhanced Modified Ludzack Ettinger-oxic Settling Anaerobic Process (E-MLE-OSA) for Treating Real Municipal Wastewater
auteurs: , Behzad Nikpour, Reza Jalilzadeh Yengejeh, , Afshin Takdastan, , Amir Hessam Hassani,
source: Journal of Advances in Environmental Health Research
resume_source: Background: Wastewater collection, treatment, discharge, additionally as reusing the treated wastewater in urban are critical factors for maintaining public health preventing contamination of water resources. This study aimed to investigate the performance of enhanced modified Ludzack Ettinger process-oxic settling anaerobic (MLE-OSA) process for treating real municipal wastewater in Sari wastewater Treatment, Sari City, Iran. Methods: To combine the OSA process technique with the MLE system, the Sludge Holding Tanks (SHT) were implemented in the return sludge line of designed pilot studies which comprised 1) MLE, which was regarded as the control system similar; 2) MLE-OSA4 with a 70-L SHT operated at 4-h Hydraulic Retention Time (HRT), and 3) MLEOSA6 with a 107-L SHT operated at 6-h HRT. To start the process, the overflow effluent of the primary settling tank of the Sari wastewater treatment plant was used. After 45-60 days, the reactors reached a steady state. The parameters of Dissolved Oxygen (DO), Oxidation-Reduction Potential (ORP), temperature, pH, Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD), Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD5), Total Suspended Solids (TSS), and nutrients were analyzed. Results: The results revealed that the average TSS, COD, BOD, phosphorus, nitrite, nitrate, and total nitrogen in MLEOSA4 effluent decreased 20.1, 14.6, 2.97, 10, 51.1, 19.3, and 20.7%, respectively compared to MLE. Similarly, in MLE-OSA6, the values decreased 34.2, 16.1, 14.6, 16.7, 69.6, 31.3, and 25.8%, respectively compared to the control process. Conclusion: Therefore, using natural wastewater, t...

titre: The Effects of Relaxing Music on Life Distress and Maternal-fetal Attachment in Pregnant Women
auteurs: , Mona Shokri Shams, Anahita Khodabakhshi-Koolaee, , Mohammad Reza Falsafinejad,
resume_source: Background: Although pregnancy and motherhood are enjoyable experiences, they are associated with numerous biopsychological changes requiring adaptation. The present study aimed to assess the effects of relaxing music on life distress and Maternal-Fetal Attachment (MFA) in pregnant women. Methods: This was a quasi-experimental study with a pre-test, post-test and a control group design. The research population included all Iranian pregnant women referring to Laleh Hospital in Tehran City, Iran, in 2020. In total, 30 women were selected using the convenience sampling method and randomly assigned into the intervention and control groups (n=15/group). The required data were collected using the Life Distress Inventory (LDI) and the Maternal-Fetal Attachment Scale (MFAS). The intervention group listened to relaxing music for twelve 45-50-minute sessions in the morning and during routine midwifery visits; however, the controls received no intervention. The collected data were analyzed using Multivariate Analysis of Covariance (MANCOVA) in SPSS V. 22. Results: The obtained results indicated that the intervention group reported a lower level of life distress in the post-test, compared to the controls (P=0.0001, F=15.860). The intervention group also achieved a higher mean score on MFA, than the control group (P=0.0001, F=35.872). Conclusion: According to the present research findings, reproductive health, nursing professionals, and psychologists could recommend music as a complementary therapy to reduce stress and distress experienced by expecting mothers and to improve MFA.

titre: Effects of Integrative Behavioral Couple Therapy on Infertility Self-efficacy, Dyadic Adjustment, and Sexual Satisfaction in Infertile Couples
auteurs: , Fatemeh Vazirnia, Javad Karimi, , Kourosh Goodarzi, , Masoud Sadeghi,
resume_source: Background: Given the rising rate of infertility, the prevalence of mental health disorders in infertile couples is undeniable. The present study aimed to investigate the effects of Integrative Behavioral Couple Therapy (IBCT) on infertility self-efficacy, dyadic adjustment, and sexual satisfaction in infertile couples. Methods: The present single-case experimental study used a multiple-baseline design. The statistical population of the study included all infertile couples referring to infertility centers in Ahvaz City, Iran, in 2019. The research instruments included the Infertility Self-Efficacy Scale (ISE), the Dyadic Adjustment Scale (DAS), and the Sexual Satisfaction Questionnaire (SSQ). Following a diagnostic interview, 3 couples were selected using the convenience sampling technique. Integrative behavioral couple therapy was conducted in twelve 120-minute sessions for the intervention group. The second couple entered the study in the second session of the first couple; the third couple enrolled the treatment plan in the third session of the first couple and the second session of the second couple. All questionnaires were completed in the first, third, sixth, eighth, and tenth sessions; the study participants were followed up and re-assessed two months later. The collected data were analyzed in SPSS using chart analysis, reliable change index, and significance statistics. Results: The provided IBCT increased infertility self-efficacy (39.04%), dyadic adjustment (25.91%), and sexual satisfaction (55.01%) in infertile couples. titre: The Relationship Between Perfectionism, Early Maladaptive Schemas, Attachment Styles, and Body Image Concern by the Mediating Role of Self-esteem in Cosmetic Surgery Applicants
auteurs: , Fatemeh Moghadam, Hossein Ebrahimi Moghadam, , Pantea Jahangir,
resume_source: Background: Psychological characteristics could significantly impact applications for cosmetic surgery as well as precognition and satisfaction with surgery. The present study aimed to investigate the relationship between perfectionism, early maladaptive schemas, attachment styles, and body image concern by the mediating role of self-esteem in cosmetic surgery applicants. Methods: This was a predictive correlational study. The statistical population of the study included all female applicants for cosmetic surgery referring to cosmetic surgery centers in Tehran City, Iran, in 2020. A sample size of 400 women was selected based on Klein’s model (2016). The required data were collected by Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (RSES) (1989), Multidimensional Perfectionism Scale (MPS), Young Schema Questionnaire (YSQ-S3), Adult Attachment Scale (AAS), and Body Image Concern Inventory (BICI), and analyzed using Pearson correlation coefficient and structural equations in SPSS and AMOS. Results: The obtained results signified a significant relationship between perfectionism, early maladaptive schemas, attachment styles, self-esteem, and body image concerns (P<0.01). Furthermore, the modified model presented a good fit (The Root Mean Square Error of Approximation (RMSEA) =0.061, GFI=0.989, IFI=0.987, P<0.05); the indirect paths of perfectionism, early maladaptive schema, and attachment styles through self-esteem were also significant. Conclusion: The evaluated model indicated a good fit; thus, it can play an essential role in recognizing the factors affecting the body image concerns of ...

titre: Comparing of the Effects of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy and Emotion Regulation Training on Diabetes Empowerment
auteurs: , Elham Eghrari, Mohammad Hossein Bayazi, , Ali Reza Rajayi,
resume_source: Background: Diabetes mellitus is a widely diffused chronic condition that affects several aspects of patients’ lives. The patient’s life in this condition depends on diabetes management ability. Therefore, this study aimed to compare the effects of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) and Emotion Regulation Training (ERT) on the diabetes empowerment of patients with type 2 diabetes. Methods: This was a quasi-experimental study with a pre-test, post-test-follow-up and a control group design. Of the statistical population of patients referring to the Diabetes Prevention and Control Center of Mashhad Province, Iran, 45 subjects were recruited by convenience sampling method; they were randomly assigned into three groups of ACT, ERT, and control (n=15/group). The study subjects were assessed using the Diabetes Empowerment Scale (F-DES-28) in the pre-test stage, after the intervention, and 3 months later. The obtained data were analyzed by repeated-measures Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) in SPSS V. 22. Results: Both provided interventions presented a significant effect on the empowerment of the research subjects, compared to the controls (P<0.001). The effectiveness of ACT on the diabetes empowerment of patients was significantly higher than that of the ERT group (P=0.04). Conclusion: It is recommended to use ACT and ERT to empower patients with type 2 diabetes.

titre: Advanced Practice Nursing Development Within Diverse Regulatory Landscapes: A Descriptive Survey of European Countries.
auteurs: Bohlender C, Bjøro K, Gill P, Unsworth J.
resume_source: Aim To explore the relationship between professional regulatory systems and advanced practice nursing development in Europe. Background Advanced practice nursing has expanded rapidly, yet regulatory frameworks have often struggled to keep pace with the extended scope of practice demanded by contemporary service delivery. Misalignment leaves new roles inadequately supported, with consequences for both patient safety and the broader transformative potential of the profession. Methods For this cross-sectional descriptive study, key informants were recruited by purposive sampling across the World Health Organization's Europe Office member countries, including regulators, educators and nursing association representatives. A purpose-built questionnaire was analysed using descriptive statistics and pattern comparison. Results The majority of European countries have advanced practice nursing roles, yet scope of practice and accompanying regulatory mechanisms varied considerably. Independent prescribing authority was the least commonly reported characteristic, having been established in only four countries. An observed descriptive pattern indicated that role maturity was related to government-led or statutory regulation designed specifically to address extended clinical skills. Interest-holders were largely in favour of regulatory intervention. Conclusion Regulatory modernisation is a key step for health systems seeking to expand advanced practice nursing. Legal scopes of practice must be realigned with clinical realities. In this sample, reported independent prescribing authority c...

titre: Supporting nurse practitioner autonomy: A policy proposal to advance hospice nurse practitioner scope.
auteurs: Hochart L, Gadler T.
resume_source: The nurse practitioner (NP) profession has achieved many advancements in its autonomy and scope of practice in the last 61 years since becoming a recognized advanced practice registered nursing role. However, some areas of health care still limit the NP's ability to practice autonomously although it is within their scope of practice. This is notable in the subspecialty of hospice care regarding certifying a terminal diagnosis as part of eligibility determination for a Medicare beneficiary to be able to receive covered hospice services. This health policy paper reviews current hospice regulations and provides evidence to support the benefits of advancing NP scope of practice and autonomy to include the ability to certify terminal diagnoses as defined in federal hospice care regulation 42 C.F.R. § 418.22. The goal of this health policy paper is successful change in federal legislation, allowing NPs to practice to the full extent of their scope and improving access to the provision of hospice care.

titre: Cochlear Implantation in a Child With Arnold-Chiari Syndrome, Severe Inner Ear Malformations, and Cochlear Nerve Hypoplasia: A Case Report.
auteurs: Skarżyński PH, Chodkiewicz A, Czajka N, Skarżyński H.
resume_source: BACKGROUND Arnold-Chiari syndrome is a congenital malformation of the posterior cranial fossa associated with neurological and otoneurological abnormalities, including hearing loss of variable severity. Cochlear implantation in patients with complex central nervous system malformations remains challenging due to uncertain auditory outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility and early outcomes of cochlear implantation in a child with Arnold-Chiari syndrome and severe bilateral inner ear malformations. CASE REPORT A 1.5-year-old girl with Arnold-Chiari malformation, hydrocephalus, spina bifida, and profound bilateral sensorineural hearing loss was evaluated for cochlear implantation. Imaging studies revealed severe bilateral inner ear malformations, including cochlear hypoplasia, accompanied by multiple intracranial abnormalities. Despite early hearing aid use, auditory development remained limited. The patient underwent left-sided cochlear implantation with a MED-EL SYNCHRONY 2 device using a standard electrode array. Intraoperatively, significant cerebrospinal fluid leakage ("gusher") occurred during cochleostomy and was successfully controlled using autologous tissues and tissue adhesive. Twelve months after implantation, follow-up audiological evaluation demonstrated improved behavioral auditory responses and increased responsiveness to environmental sounds, as reported by the parents. CONCLUSIONS Cochlear implantation may provide meaningful auditory benefit in selected patients with Arnold-Chiari syndrome despite severe inner ear and central nervous system abn...

titre: Antifungal ototoxicity, itraconazole, and approaches to its mitigation: a review of a sparse evidence base.
auteurs: Vališ M, Juklová K, Skorunková R, Frydrych Š, Halúsková S.
resume_source: 1. introduction Hearing loss is a recognised hazard of aminoglycosides and platinum chemotherapy, but the auditory risk of antifungal drugs has received far less attention. Itraconazole lists hearing loss in its prescribing information, yet dedicated peer-reviewed auditory studies appear absent. 2. areas covered The original 139-record Web of Science (WoS) title-only corpus was retained to map the wider ototoxicity field. A targeted WoS Topic-field sensitivity search using antifungal-specific terms and broader auditory outcomes retrieved 153 records, of which 18 direct antifungal auditory safety/toxicity studies were retained. No dedicated auditory study of itraconazole was identified. The expanded evidence shows formulation- and route-dependent topical effects, a pharmacovigilance signal for oral terbinafine, no auditory brainstem response shift in a short-duration animal study of systemic voriconazole or caspofungin, and rare hearing-loss reports plus a pharmacovigilance signal for amphotericin B. Otoprotection evidence from other drug classes is considered for transferable mitigation principles. 3. expert opinion The broader search shows a heterogeneous but sparse evidence base rather than an absence of evidence. Human systemic azole data remain particularly limited, and itraconazole lacks dedicated auditory investigation. Baseline and serial audiometry, separation of drug effects from infection and interacting medicines, and mechanistic studies are priorities.

titre: Demystifying credentialing and privileging for clinical nurse specialists.
auteurs: Archer M.
resume_source: Abstract A clinical nurse specialist (CNS) is an advanced practice registered nurse who holds a graduate degree and specializes in managing specific patient populations or disease types, bringing advanced clinical expertise to diagnose, treat, and oversee care for individuals and improve population health conditions. CNSs serve as clinical leaders, educators, and practitioners of evidence-based care, driving improvements in patient outcomes and instigating transformational organizational change within health care systems. Their scope of practice is broad, encompassing assessment, care coordination, consultation, and, where permitted, prescribing and procedural privileges, all founded upon rigorous academic and clinical standards. The process of credentialing ensures that CNSs meet established educational, training, licensure, and competency criteria before providing care, while privileging authorizes them to perform specialized clinical activities within health care facilities. Unfortunately, CNSs often face regulatory and institutional barriers, such as misclassification, restrictive state laws, and inconsistent privileging criteria, which undermine their ability to fully utilize their advanced skills and impede the recognition of their contributions. Such obstacles can limit professional growth and restrict independent practice and reimbursement opportunities. This article discusses credentialing, privileging, mapping, patient encounters, and workload for CNSs, who are often overlooked and underutilized in advanced practice conversations despite providing safe, high-quali...

titre: Beyond the silo: Single-disorder ADHD clinics and the case for more integrated care.
auteurs: Das S, Chatterjee SS.
resume_source: ObjectiveThe rapid growth of ADHD assessment and prescribing in Australia reflects a gap between demand and service availability. Workforce shortages, restrictive stimulant regulations and limited adult ADHD care within public mental health services have contributed to this gap. ADHD-focused clinics have emerged in response. Using two de-identified clinical scenarios, this paper examines the drivers of this model and its potential harms.ConclusionFocused clinics can improve access and provide expertise. However, a narrow scope and fee-for-service model may also encourage transactional and fragmented care. We describe this risk as organisational iatrogenesis. Potential harms include incomplete formulation, uncoordinated prescribing and missed psychiatric, neurodevelopmental or neurocognitive comorbidity. Broader concerns include inequity, cost, discontinuity of care and erosion of generalist skills. The solution is not to restrict focused practice, but to integrate it more effectively with mainstream care. Priorities include nationally consistent prescribing rules, stronger shared-care arrangements with general practitioners, greater adult ADHD capacity within public services and clearer standards for scope-restricted practice. These issues are also relevant to other single-disorder models of psychiatric care.

titre: Literary Element Use in Written Narratives for Third-Grade Children Who Are Deaf and Hard of Hearing.
auteurs: Grey B, Lund EA, Werfel KL.
resume_source: Purpose This study examined literary element use in third-grade written narratives to determine if children who are deaf and hard of hearing (DHH) and their peers with typical hearing (TH) met macrostructure writing proficiency expectations addressed in the Common Core State Standards. Method Participants included 134 children who completed third grade across three groups: children who used cochlear implants (CIs), children who used hearing aids (HAs), and children with TH. Given a picture prompt, participants composed a written narrative. Using the third-grade Common Core State Standards that addressed macrostructure, written narratives were scored with a rubric that outlined the criteria for meeting seven literary element categories: characters, actions, feelings, dialogue, topic, sequence, and plot. Results CI, HA, and TH children did not meet most macrostructure literary element criteria for narrative writing addressed in the third-grade Common Core State Standards. Literary element outcomes did not significantly differ between CI, HA, and TH groups, except for topic. Conclusions DHH and TH third-grade students did not demonstrate strong macrostructure writing skills in their written narratives. To build a solid writing foundation, elementary students, regardless of hearing status, would benefit from general and genre-specific writing interventions that incorporate self-regulating strategies throughout their writing process to facilitate the transition from learning to write to writing to learn. Supplemental material https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.34259406.

titre: Nurses Have Always Diagnosed: The Historical, Legal and Scientific Case for Nursing Engagement in Diagnosis.
auteurs: Harkless GE, Gleason KT, Jefferies C.
resume_source: Aim To review the historical, legal, theoretical and evidentiary foundations for registered nurse engagement in diagnosis and to argue for systematic inclusion of nursing's diagnostic contributions in team-based diagnosis. Background Diagnosis has been a constitutive element of nursing practice since the profession's earliest years, yet nursing's diagnostic authority has been persistently contested, constrained by legislation and rendered invisible in health information systems and diagnostic safety frameworks. Design Discursive paper. Methods Drawing on published research, regulatory and historical analysis, and interprofessional policy literature, the paper traces nursing's diagnostic role from early public health nursing through legislation, case law and standardized nursing language, and current evidence on diagnostic safety and education. Results Nursing diagnosis is not a novel aspiration or an expansion of scope but a documented feature of practice across more than a century; as Christman and Safriet argued, no discipline owns knowledge, and diagnostic language serves the patient, not professional territory. Team-based diagnosis including nurses improves quality and reduces error, yet scope-of-practice barriers and a preparation-to-practice gap in clinical judgement constrain nursing's contribution. Conclusion Systematic inclusion of nursing's diagnostic contributions is essential to achieving high-quality, equitable, team-based diagnosis. Realizing this requires removing regulatory and structural barriers and strengthening nurses' preparation in clinical reasoning a...

titre: Impacted Fetal Head at Cesarean Birth: A Clinical Nursing Review.
auteurs: Atkisson JL.
resume_source: Abstract Fetal head impaction (IFH) occurs when the presenting part becomes wedged in the maternal pelvis during a cesarean section, requiring additional maneuvers to complete birth. As cesarean rates have risen, so has IFH, estimated to occur in 1.5% of all births annually in the United States. Maternal complications include uterine extension, hemorrhage, bladder injury, and intensive care unit admission. Neonatal complications include low cord pH, skull fracture, intracranial hemorrhage, hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, and death. These outcomes are not inevitable. Management technique, clinician education, and interdisciplinary institutional preparation are modifiable factors with direct bearing on outcomes when IFH is encountered. Despite its frequency and consequence, the topic of IFH and the role of the nurse are absent from nursing education, professional standards, and scope-of-practice guidance. A search of CINAHL, PubMed, Ovid, and EBSCO identified no peer-reviewed nursing literature addressing IFH or its intraoperative management. Labor and delivery nurses commonly report first encountering manual vaginal disimpaction when urgently asked to perform it during an emergency, without education, competence validation, or institutional policy. Improving outcomes requires institutional infrastructure built before any individual emergency, and professional nursing organizations must clarify where manual vaginal disimpaction falls within nursing scope of practice.

titre: Longitudinal Growth of Mandated Hearing Aid Benefits in the US.

Prior research has examined private insurance and Medicaid mandates separately, leaving the overall reach of coverage across all major US programs unclear. Objective To identify mandated hearing aid coverage under private insurance, Medicaid, and federal direct-service programs and to compare coverage for US youth, adults, and older adults by coverage plan and economic indicators. Design, setting, and participants This cross-sectional study used population-level policy surveillance data with nationally representative insurance data from the American Community Survey (ACS) from 2008 to 2023. ACS respondents were categorized by age (younger than 18 years, 18 to 64 years, and 65 years or older), insurance type (state-level private insurance, Medicaid, and federal direct-service insurance providers), and eligibility for hearing aid coverage. Data were analyzed from February 2024 to August 2026. Exposures Mandated health coverage for hearing aids through private insurers, Medicaid, US Department of Veterans Affairs, TRICARE, and Indian Health Service. titre: Jervell and Lange-Nielsen Syndrome
auteurs: Faridi R, Przybylski R, Saenen J, Hertzano R, Newman WG, Friedman TB.
resume_source: Clinical characteristics Jervell and Lange-Nielsen syndrome (JLNS) is characterized by bilateral sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL), vestibular dysfunction, and QTc prolongation on repeated testing. Iron deficiency anemia may be present in some people with KCNQ1 pathogenic variants. The hearing loss is most often congenital and severe to profound, although milder degrees of hearing loss have been described. Temporal bone anatomy on CT is normal. Vestibular dysfunction may result in gross motor delay (including later ages of walking), balance impairment, and absent physiologic nystagmus. In the absence of other reversible conditions that prolong the QT interval, serial 12-lead surface electrocardiograms show a prolonged QTc interval using the Bazzet formula exceeding 450 ms in prepubertal children, 460 ms in adult men, and 470 ms in adult women or a high probability long QT syndrome (LQTS) score ≥3.5. Repeated QTc prolongation must be observed, as a large overlap exists between unaffected individuals and those with LQTS. In KCNQ1-JLNS1, QTc prolongation is often severe (>500 ms) and associated with high risk for ventricular arrhythmias (e.g., torsade de pointes that can spontaneously resolve or degenerate into ventricular fibrillation), which if left untreated may result in syncope or sudden cardiac death (SCD). In KCNE1-JLNS2, QTc prolongation is reported to be less severe, though significant risk for malignant ventricular arrhythmias remains. titre: Task force of the Brazilian Society of Otology and the Brazilian Academy of Neurotology: Menière's Disease.
auteurs: Pauna HF, Silva VAR, Lavinsky J, de Giacomo Carneiro C, Mangia LRL, Grasel SS, de Oliveira Beck RM, Salmito MC, de Carvalho Lopes K, Mezzalira R, Furtado PL, Sampaio ALL, Mano PM, Bertoldo C, de Carvalho RCB, Joffily L, de Rezende Oliveira LN, Lamounier P, Selaimen FA, Lavinsky L, Lopes da Silva MN,...
resume_source: Objective To critically review the available evidence on the pathophysiology and diagnosis of Menière's disease and to provide consensus-based recommendations developed by a task force of the Brazilian Society of Otology and the Brazilian Academy of Neurotology. Methods A task force consisting of experts in otology and neurotology was established to review the scientific literature and develop thematic sections of the document. The content was discussed in both in-person and remote meetings until consensus was achieved. Recommendations were graded according to level of evidence and strength of recommendation using standardized systems for the evaluation of therapeutic interventions and diagnostic methods. Results Menière's disease is a heterogeneous clinical condition characterized by recurrent episodes of vertigo, fluctuating sensorineural hearing loss, tinnitus, and aural fullness. Endolymphatic hydrops represents the most consistent histopathologic finding; however, it does not alone explain the clinical expression of the disease. Current evidence indicates the involvement of multifactorial mechanisms, including genetic predisposition, immune dysfunction, inflammatory processes, and changes in inner ear ion homeostasis. Diagnosis remains primarily clinical, based on international criteria, with serial audiometry playing a key role. Electrophysiologic testing and imaging may be useful in selected situations. titre: The Relationship among Obesity, Intracranial Hypertension, and Cerebrospinal Fluid Leak.
auteurs: Ojeda-Badillo G, Naples JG.
resume_source: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) is a disorder characterized by elevated intracranial pressure without identifiable lesion or secondary cause. Patients can often present with otolaryngologic manifestations of IIH, such as pulsatile tinnitus, aural fullness, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak. Obesity plays an important role as a risk factor for both IIH and CSF leak as similar pathophysiological processes underly both presentations. Understanding the nuanced presentation of this condition is important for the otolaryngologist who routinely evaluates patients with these symptoms and has implications for management decisions. In this article, we discuss the relationship among obesity, IIH, and CSF leak.

titre: The history of tinnitus: from ancient interpretations to contemporary neuroscience and neuromodulation.
auteurs: William R.
resume_source: Objective To review the historical evolution of tinnitus from ancient civilizations to contemporary neuromodulation-based therapies. Methods A narrative historical review was undertaken using PubMed, Google Scholar, historical archives, classical medical texts, and landmark otological publications. Sources were selected according to historical significance, relevance to tinnitus, and contribution to major shifts in its conceptualisation and management. Results As a non-systematic narrative review, this study traces the conceptual paradigm shifts in tinnitus understanding. Early civilizations attributed tinnitus to supernatural causes, while Greek and Islamic scholars introduced humoral and clinical theories. The nineteenth century established scientific otology, rooting tinnitus in peripheral ear pathology. Crucially, modern neuroscience prompted a paradigm shift from these peripheral cochlear models to central network theories. This shift has driven the exploration of specific neuromodulation modalities, such as repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) and bimodal stimulation. Conclusion The history of tinnitus reflects the broader evolution of medicine, progressing from superstition to evidence-based neuro-otological science.

Methods Six databases were searched from 1990 to 2023 (2025 updated) for randomized clinical trials, observational studies, and case studies with at least one group receiving invasive or non-invasive VNS with sound for tinnitus management. Eligible studies used validated questionnaires to quantify tinnitus distress or severity in patients compared with controls or pre-treatment status. Two reviewers extracted participant, intervention, blinding, assessment, and outcome data. The risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I for non-randomized studies and ROB2 for randomized controlled trials. PRISMA guidelines were followed. titre: Consumer preferences for hearing health care information and services as described by older adults surveyed in Australia, Canada, England, and the United States.
auteurs: Alnafjan F, Davis AC, Lee ML, McMahon CM, Mokdad AH, Mosley CL, Pichora-Fuller MK, Tremblay KL.
resume_source: Background Age-related hearing loss is a global public health concern and yet hearing health care (HHC) services remain underutilized. Understanding the HHC experiences of older adults is essential to addressing why existing systems are underutilized. Therefore, we surveyed older adults to determine their preferences for HHC service delivery. In this cross-sectional survey study, we report where they preferred to obtain HHC information, undergo hearing tests, and acquire hearing devices. We also examined whether these preferences varied by degree of hearing loss, help-seeking experience, survey mode (online or in person), age, or country. Methods Using survey questions that were co-created with consumers, responses were collected online and in person prior to the pandemic (2016-2018) in the United States (USA), Canada (CAN), Australia (AUS), and England (EN). Third-party firms recruited convenience samples from each region. Participants, aged 60 + and proficient in English, responded to three questions: "Where would you prefer to get information about HHC?" (8,151 respondents, 14 response options), "Where would you most like to get your hearing tested?" (8,035 respondents, 8 options), and "From which of the following places would you MOST like to get hearing aids (or other types of hearing devices) if you needed them?" (8,151 respondents, 11 options). Participants could select multiple options. titre: [Chances and challenges in the prevention and treatment of early childhood hearing loss: the AWMF guideline on congenital CMV infection].
auteurs: Kummer P, Buxmann H, Roll C, Enders M, Goelz R, Modrow S, Leitlinien-Gruppe S2k Leitlinie „Zytomegalievirus-Infektion (CMV)“.
resume_source: After genetic causes, congenital cytomegalovirus (cCMV) infection is the leading infectious cause of congenital and early childhood hearing loss. The 2025 German S2k guideline on prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of CMV infection in pregnant women and congenital CMV infection in neonates and children published by the Association of the Scientific Medical Societies in Germany (Arbeitsgemeinschaft der Wissenschaftlichen Medizinischen Fachgesellschaften, AWMF; 093-003 [24]) provides corresponding recommendations and summarizes the current evidence. Hygiene counseling of pregnant women, targeted diagnostic testing during pregnancy and in neonates, and antiviral therapeutic options are important measures for prevention and treatment of congenital CMV infection. Universal newborn hearing screening (UNHS) is decisive for the diagnosis of congenital hearing loss. If abnormal results are revealed in the initial and follow-up testing, polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis of CMV DNA in urine (gold standard) or saliva should be performed immediately-as it should be in the case of other symptoms-preferably in the maternity or pediatric hospital and certainly not later than in the second to third week of life. In the case of symptomatic congenital CMV infection, causal treatment of congenital hearing loss can be offered as early as during the first 30 days of life-both for clinically symptomatic infants and for those with isolated hearing loss. titre: Ear-Worn Inertial Measurement of Sit-to-Stand and Sit-to-Walk Movements: Algorithm Development and Validation.
auteurs: Fawden T, Edwards A, Roberts IV, Dunne H, Stone T, Bance M.
resume_source: Background Sit-to-stand and sit-to-walk are common functional movements that provide insight into an individual's functional mobility. Developing comprehensive measures of these movements using ear-worn inertial measurement units (IMUs), which are increasingly incorporated into widely used devices such as hearing aids and headphones, could provide a means of monitoring older adults and individuals with movement disorders with minimal additional burden. Objective This paper aimed to introduce comprehensive outcome measures for sit-to-stand and sit-to-walk movements based on data from ear-worn IMUs, and to evaluate their agreement with an optical motion capture reference. Methods Data were analyzed from 62 participants, of whom 46 (18 male and 28 female; median age 27, IQR 15 years) did not have a known underlying movement condition and 16 (7 male and 9 female; median age 62, IQR 23 years) did. The participants wore a bespoke 3D-printed headset that contained 6-axis IMUs placed beside their left and right ears. A reflective marker was placed on each participant's seventh cervical vertebra to provide an optical motion capture reference. Each participant performed 3 sit-to-stand movements and 3 sit-to-walk movements. The reported outcome metrics included overall and subphase durations, acceleration, velocity, power, movement smoothness, and hesitation. titre: Cochlear Implant Training in Doctor of Audiology Programs: A Survey Study.
auteurs: Hall M, Windmill I, Sprouse B, Zwolan T.
resume_source: Purpose As the population of cochlear implant (CI) candidates and recipients grows, there is a need for more audiologists to meet their clinical needs. Little information exists regarding the perception of recent doctorate of audiology (AuD) graduates and the training they received related to CI. Method We surveyed audiologists who graduated from an accredited AuD program between 2017 and 2023 and asked them several questions about their level of satisfaction regarding their AuD studies. The survey included questions about current work setting, areas of rotation available, and instructor characteristics related to areas in the AuD. Results Respondents demonstrated high levels of satisfaction with their AuD training overall; 93% reported they were "very" or "somewhat" satisfied. Sixty-three percent reported they were "completely" or "somewhat satisfied" with the training related to CI. Most dissatisfied respondents reported that this was due to limited opportunities for hands-on work with the CI population. Seventy-two percent indicated they were "very" or "somewhat satisfied" with their CI instructor, and many tended to report higher satisfaction when instructors were clinicians with practical experience. CI rotations with adults were more prevalent than pediatric CI placements, and both were rated as less available than pediatric and adult hearing aids and diagnostic testing. A significant number of recent graduates reported gaps in their learning of topics related to insurance, reimbursement, billing, and coding. titre: Cochlear Implant Referrals in Adults With Severe-to-Profound Hearing Loss in the United Kingdom (CIRCA-2): Protocol for a Repeat National Multicenter Retrospective Observational Study.
auteurs: North AS, Swords C, Checkland P, Daniels J, Denton OG, Habeeb A, Lim KH, Jarratt-Barnham I, Rajgor A, Tailor BV, Wong J, Muzaffar J.
resume_source: Background Cochlear implantation (CI) is a highly effective intervention for adults with severe-to-profound hearing loss, yet uptake across the United Kingdom remains low despite clear National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE 2019) guidance and well-established clinical benefits. The original Cochlear Implant Referral Criteria Audit (CIRCA-1) identified marked inequities in access to CIs in 2022, with lower referral rates among older adults, males, and individuals from socioeconomically deprived areas, alongside individuals from minority ethnic backgrounds being less likely to be informed of their eligibility for referral. Since then, national awareness initiatives and the expansion of the existing local "CI Champions" scheme have aimed to address these inequities, improve awareness of CI candidacy, and improve the quality of discussions with patients about options for CI referral. This repeat assessment aims to assess the success of these interventions to identify improvements in access to CIs as well as persisting barriers. Objective CIRCA-2 is a national, multicenter, retrospective observational audit designed to re-evaluate adult CI referral pathways and measure progress since the first audit cycle. Methods The study will include adults assessed in secondary-care ear, nose, throat, and audiology departments between July and December 2025 whose audiometric thresholds meet NICE TA566 criteria. titre: Determinants of auditory performance after cochlear implantation in post-lingual adults: beyond the duration of hearing loss.
auteurs: Caride M, Almeida J.
resume_source: Purpose Prolonged auditory deprivation progressively compromises central auditory pathway integrity, yet its prognostic impact in post-lingual adults undergoing cochlear implantation remains poorly defined. This study evaluates the influence of hearing loss duration - expressed in absolute terms, dichotomised by the conventional 10-year threshold, and as a proportion of lifetime with hearing loss - on auditory performance, and identifies the clinical determinants associated with the immediate activation effect and the post-implantation trajectory. Methods Single-centre, retrospective, observational study at Unidade Local de Saúde de Santo António, including 109 post-lingual adults undergoing CI between 2018 and 2024, with a minimum follow-up of 12 months. Auditory performance was assessed through pure-tone average, speech reception threshold, and speech discrimination score. Longitudinal modelling used linear mixed-effects models, distinguishing the immediate activation effect from subsequent temporal progression. Results Patients with longer hearing loss duration presented greater pre-implantation auditory impairment across all metrics, following a continuous dose-response relationship with no evidence of a threshold effect. The 10-year criterion showed no discriminative value - either in the immediate effect or in the post-implantation trajectory, which was equivalent between groups. titre: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Over-the-Counter Hearing Aids in Ageing Populations With Hearing Loss.
auteurs: Kim GY, Jo M, Cho YS, Lee S, Moon IJ.
resume_source: Background and objectives Hearing loss (HL) is common among older adults and associated with adverse health outcomes. Although hearing aids (HAs) are effective for mild to moderately severe HL, their use is limited by cost and stigma. To improve accessibility, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has authorized over-the-counter (OTC) HAs. This study compared the performance of OTC HAs with that of prescription HAs in older adults with mild-to-moderate HL. Subjects and methods In this prospective cohort study, 30 older adults were evaluated using six HA models: one prescription HA (ReSound ONE) and five OTC HAs (Lexie B2, Vibe Air, Vibe Nano8, Jabra Enhance Plus, and Olive Smart Ear Plus). The effectiveness was assessed using sound field audiometry, word recognition scores (WRS), speech perception in noise (SPIN), and real-ear measurements (REMs). Repeated-measures analysis of variance was used for the analysis. Results Significant primary effects of the auditory test (p Conclusions OTC HAs demonstrated a performance comparable to that of prescription HAs and may serve as a cost-effective option for older adults with mild-to-moderate HL.
